newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatists say too soon to end violence.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatists say too soon to end violence.

text.p: Leaders of a Corsican separatist group concluded on Sunday that it was too soon to end their violent campaign for increased autonomy from mainland France despite a government crackdown on their movement.

"The conditions for an end to political violence are not yet in place," Jean-Guy Talamoni, spokesman for the A Cuncolta Naziunalista separatist group, told reporters after a strategy meeting at a secret location on the French Mediterranean island.
The group is the political arm of the Historic Wing of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), which has been battling for two decades for greater autonomy.

Separatist guerrillas regularly stage bombing attacks on the island. Two bombs exploded overnight on Sunday, damaging a driving school and a bank but causing no casualties, police said. No one immediately claimed responsibity for those blasts.

The government has announced a crackdown on the violence, which has cut deeply into island tourist revenues. Some separatist groups have in response escalated their campaign by attacking targets in mainland France, including the Bordeaux city hall where Prime Minister Alain Juppe sits as mayor.
Three leaders of the A Cuncolta Naziunalista group have surrendered to police in recent weeks and others have been arrested, triggering the strategy session.
Talamoni denounced the wave of arrests and said justice officials had no evidence of wrongdoing by its members.
He said the group was considering filing a complaint with a Paris human rights organisation against the tactics used by French law enforcement authorities.
In an unrelated action, Corsican farmers continued to tie up roads and petrol stations on the island to press demands for a rescheduling of debts and other state aid.
Groups of farmers had last week occupied the island's two petrol depots to dramatise their demands but were forcibly ejected from the depots by police on Friday.
After that, they put up roadblocks around the island to block traffic and attempted to intimidate island petrol station owners to discourage them from keeping their stations open.
Farmers' union representatives called for a demonstration on Monday in the southern island city of Ajaccio and were expected to meet Agriculture Ministry officials in Paris.
